defects: f is typed as ℕ → ℝ instead of ℝ → ℝ; the theorem no longer refers to a genuine real-valued function on the continuum, changing the fundamental structure of the integral test
hf_antitone requires Antitone f globally on all of ℕ, whereas gold only requires AntitoneOn f (Ici N), i.e. eventual (from N onward) monotonicity — a strictly stronger/different hypothesis
hf_nonneg requires nonnegativity for all n : ℕ, whereas gold only requires nonnegativity on Ioi N — again stronger/different than gold's eventual condition

the integrability hypothesis is stated for the step function fun x => f (Int.natAbs ⌊x⌋) rather than for f itself; since this step function is constant on each [k,k+1), its integrability on Ioi N is essentially equivalent to absolute summability of f over ℕ, making the hypothesis nearly equivalent to the conclusion itself and trivializing the theorem instead of expressing the genuine integral-test comparison between ∫f and ∑f(n)
conclusion sums a native ℕ → ℝ function directly rather than the restriction (fun n => f n) of a ℝ → ℝ function, compounding the domain mismatch with gold
